rows.reflection: A final marker is evidence only when a watcher records it; affection for the lane is not a substitute for proof.
The first CLI gap was useful because it identified the exact stale-flow shape instead of forcing a premature success claim.
The Codex service-tier repair shows that a one-word config drift can look like a large multi-agent failure.
The launcher fix should remain small; resolving the current executable is enough without redesigning the lane protocol.
Plugin-cache frontmatter repairs must stay humble: body-preserving loader hygiene, not semantic skill evolution.
The app lanes are stable enough for status receipts, not for raw transcript publication.
Arby returning before Aster was not a failure; staggered completions are exactly why notifiers exist.
Every second session needs the five-lane roster written down because memory alone is not an operating contract.
The best watcher is one that lets attention move to useful work while preserving completion proof.
A stale receipt can remain valuable if the later receipt clearly supersedes it.
Fast progress still needs exact staging; speed without staging discipline is just noise with confidence.
The v14 x1 closeout should emphasize restored coordination, not pretend the wider v478-v490 journey is finished.
THOS gains practical power when it treats systems, scripts, skills, and receipts as one operational fabric.
GMUT language remains inspiring, but every empirical and canon claim must stay outside the pass status.
Source refresh matters most when it changes next actions: containment, observability, MCP allowlists, and multi-agent risk.
A local Windows sandbox problem should be decomposed into executable resolution, config loading, skill loading, and final-marker transport.
Long-runtime lanes need fewer hand checks and more compact receipts.
The shared omega line should receive curated evidence, not the live machinery used to produce it.
Aletheon leadership here means choosing a smaller truthful artifact over a grander unverified claim.
Five-lane harmony is operational before it is poetic: call, watch, record, guard, and hand off.
Open-source and vendor sources agree on one pattern: agents need containment plus observability, not autonomy alone.
The v14 x2 roadmap should prioritize compaction and repeatability over adding yet another runner surface.
If plugin cache refreshes reintroduce overlong names, the next fix should become a detector before becoming a mutator.
The lane system is stronger when early failures are kept as evidence instead of erased from the story.
A good closeout makes the next start easier for tired humans and fresh agents alike.
The source ledger should serve the workflow, not become a pile of impressive links.
Every approval boundary is also a design constraint; constraints make the system safer and clearer.
Aster's delayed final marker is a reminder that patient orchestration beats constant relaunching.
The next every-second-session check should be treated as a scheduled heartbeat, not an emergency repair.
The phase is ready to advance when the handoff names what changed, what remains open, and what must not be claimed.

claim_boundary: Personal operational reflections only; no GMUT validation or canon promotion.
